◆ Portfolio view (filtered set)
Methodology. EV is split by task: direct tasks earn on revenue progress (cumulative earned revenue / total planned revenue x direct budget), while indirect tasks (task numbers starting 300) are absorbed in proportion to direct-cost progress (actual direct cost / direct budget, capped at 100%) x indirect budget. Previously EV was (cumulative earned revenue / total planned revenue) x total cost budget (BAC) -- a physical-progress proxy, since no independent % complete field was supplied. PV = time-phased Current Budget (cost) by period, from the Budget Resources by Expenditure Category file. AC = Raw Cost from the PPM cost reports. Planned revenue is the real time-phased revenue budget (Current Budget Revenue) from the Budget Resources -- Revenue file, not an estimate. Forecast tails (dashed) extrapolate the last 6 months run-rate until EAC / total planned revenue is reached. Category CPI trend applies the projects overall physical-progress % to each categorys own budget at completion, since no per-category progress % exists in the source data -- treat it as an approximation, not an independently measured figure. Subcontractor and Internal Services have no budget baseline in the Budget Resources file, so a category CPI trend cannot be computed for them. Only projects present in the budget baseline file are shown, per the requested scope. Duration and area filters change the reporting window and project set — KPI cards report figures "as of" the selected end period, not the final period, when a duration filter is active. Budget resource classes (Material Items, Financial Resources, Equipment, Labor) and actual expenditure categories (which also include Subcontractor and Internal Services) come from two different source schemas and do not map one-to-one; they are shown side by side rather than merged into a single variance figure.

Update data — monthly upload

Incorrect username or password.

Each box below is independent — upload just one when that's all you have. Parsing happens entirely in your browser; nothing is sent anywhere. Large cost files may take a minute.

1. Cost budget baseline

Budget Resources by Expenditure Category (.xlsx — select as many files as you need). Replaces the budget for every project number found across the files you pick; every other project's budget is left untouched. If a project appears in more than one file, its rows are combined.

2. Planned revenue baseline

Budget Resources by Expenditure Category — Revenue (.xlsx — select as many as you need). Same rule as above: replaces planned revenue only for the project numbers found across the files you pick.

3. Actual cost (monthly)

PPM Projects Cost Monthly Report (.xlsx — select as many as you need). Works period by period: for every project + accounting period found across the files, the old figures for that exact month are deleted and replaced by the new ones. Any month not present is left exactly as it was — nothing is removed, new months are simply added.

4. Actual revenue & billing (monthly)

Summary Invoices & Revenue By Line (.xlsx — select as many as you need). Treated the same way as actual cost above — replaced per project and period, other months untouched — since this is also month-by-month actuals data. Also refreshes each project's area tag and invoiced-lines total.

5. Budget ↔ revenue line mapping

The SAJCO_Budget_Revenue_Line_Mapping.xlsx template, with the Confirmed Revenue Line column filled in. It links budget tasks that can't be matched by task number, so they earn value on installed quantity instead of revenue progress. The latest file replaces the previous mapping. Rows left blank keep the fallback.

Save a shareable copy

Writes a new HTML file with the current data baked inside it. Send that file to anyone and it opens with this data already loaded — no upload, no browser storage needed. Use this whenever you want the data to travel with the file.
